seoTitle: Minneapolis Public Schools Calendar: MPS Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed Minneapolis Public Schools dates, first days by grade, no-school days for religious observances, MEA Break, bell-time guidance, and official PDFs in four languages.
districtFact: Minneapolis Public Schools uses a 168-day calendar with separate openings for grades 1–12 and Pre-K–K. The first day has another operational wrinkle: grades 10–12 must check their school for a possible late start while ninth-grade orientation takes place. MPS also schedules districtwide non-school days for four religious observances when they fall on an otherwise instructional date.

about.title: Two Opening Dates, Plus a High-School Time Check
about.content: Grades 1–12 begin two days before Pre-K and kindergarten in every reviewed calendar. On that first grades 1–12 date, ninth graders attend orientation while grades 10–12 are told to check their school for a later start time. Families therefore need both the district date and the student's high-school instructions.

about.title: Religious Observances Can Be Districtwide Non-School Days
about.content: The MPS School Board identifies Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr, and Eid al-Adha as non-school days when the first day of the observance would otherwise be instructional. Which observances appear on a school-year PDF changes with the calendar, so families should not carry one year's closure list into the next.

about.title: Four Published Calendar Languages
about.content: MPS publishes the 2026–27 and 2027–28 one-page calendars in English, Spanish, Somali, and Hmong. That access reflects a district where families speak more than 100 languages and where multilingual programming includes Spanish and Hmong dual-language pathways and Somali heritage language.

about.title: Community Schools and Citywide Magnets
about.content: MPS describes 50 community schools connected to Minneapolis neighborhoods and 13 centrally located magnet schools with themes such as arts, STEM, STEAM, dual language, Montessori, and global studies. Districtwide closure dates are shared, but bell times and school events remain campus-specific.

calendarNotes: MPS publishes 168 instructional days in each reviewed student calendar. Grades 1–12 begin first, followed two days later by Pre-K and kindergarten. Grades 10–12 should check their school for a later first-day start while ninth-grade orientation occurs. Family-teacher conferences are non-school days, and the two-day MEA Break follows the fall conference date. Record-keeping and professional-development dates create additional non-school days around several breaks. MPS schedules one non-school day for Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr, or Eid al-Adha when the observance falls on a planned instructional day. School start and end times vary by campus, so the district date list does not replace the official bell-time table. English, Spanish, Somali, and Hmong calendar PDFs are available for the two future years covered here.

planningTips.title: Planning with the Minneapolis Public Schools Calendar
content: Use the student's grade to choose the correct September first day; Pre-K and kindergarten start two days after grades 1–12.
For grades 10–12, confirm the first-day arrival time with the high school because ninth-grade orientation can create a later start for older students.
Combine the fall family-teacher conference with the following MEA Break when planning childcare; together they create three consecutive student-free weekdays.
Check no-school days for religious observances year by year because lunar and lunisolar dates move across the school calendar.
Use the school-level start/end-time table for transportation and care plans; MPS campuses do not share one universal bell schedule.
Treat the listed summer-school range as a separate program window, not as part of the 168-day regular school year.

Recheck official MPS messages after severe weather or School Board action because calendar modifications are communicated through district channels and a MySchoolDates import does not update automatically.

districtFaqs.q: Do all Minneapolis Public Schools students start on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. Grades 1–12 begin first, and Pre-K and kindergarten begin two days later. Grades 10–12 must also check their school for a possible late first-day start during ninth-grade orientation.

districtFaqs.q: How many instructional days are on the MPS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Each reviewed Minneapolis Public Schools student calendar lists 168 instructional days. Summer-school dates are separate from that regular-year total.

districtFaqs.q: What is MEA Break on the Minneapolis school calendar?
districtFaqs.a: MPS labels a two-day October student break as MEA Break. It follows the fall family-teacher conference day, creating a three-weekday non-school sequence.

districtFaqs.q: Which religious observances can close MPS schools?
districtFaqs.a: The MPS School Board identifies Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Eid al-Fitr, and Eid al-Adha for a non-school day when the observance falls on what would otherwise be an instructional day.

districtFaqs.q: Are Minneapolis school start times the same at every campus?
districtFaqs.a: No. MPS publishes a school-by-school start and end time table. Check your school’s current listing before making transportation or child-care plans.

districtFaqs.q: What languages are MPS school-year calendars available in?
districtFaqs.a: For 2026–27 and 2027–28, MPS publishes official calendar PDFs in English, Spanish, Somali, and Hmong.

customSections.label: How MPS Chooses Religious-Observance Closures
customSections.content: MPS says the School Board selected four observances because of significant attendance impacts for students and families. A non-school day generally applies on the first day of a multi-day observance only when that date would otherwise have been a school day. The resulting dates differ by year, which is why each calendar below lists only the closures printed for that specific year.
